content.text:
We need to choose which March order to resolve now: we have two March orders remaining for Stark: one at "the-shivering-sea" (order id 1, March -1) and one at "white-harbor" (order id 2, March +0). According to actionGuidance, we have the reachable destinations for each:

- For the-shivering-sea: reachableRegions list includes:
  - regionId: "the-narrow-sea", type: "sea", castleLevel: 0, castleAreasGainedIfCaptured:0, garrison:0, controller:null, triggersCombat:false, neutralForce:null, supplySafeUnitIdGroupsWhenChosenAlone:[[4]].
So only "the-narrow-sea"? Let's double-check the mapping. The actionGuidance indicates that for each starting region (the-shivering-sea), reachableRegions list is given. For the starting region "the-shivering-sea", reachableRegions includes only "the-narrow-sea". And canLeavePowerToken: false.

Thus with March -1 order (the-shivering-sea) we can move the unit(s) from the Shivering Sea (the unit is ID 4, type ship). It can move to the-narrow-sea (sea). There's only one unit (unit ID 4). We cannot leave power token (cannot vacate because it's sea and have no control?). Wait canLeavePowerToken false. So we cannot place a Power token to retain control of the source area? That's rarely needed for sea. Indeed we can't control sea. So early: we can move the ship to the-narrow-sea. That would be moving into a sea area that currently has no units (provided "the-narrow-sea" is empty? We need to query check_neighbours for the-narrow-sea to see if any units or orders there. Also need to see if moving there triggers combat: if there are enemy units, combat would start, but triggersCombat is false (as per guidance). But it's not a guarantee that there are no enemy units; the "triggersCombat": false suggests if you move there, you won't trigger a combat perhaps because there's no enemy unit (or it's considered just a normal movement that's not combat). Usually, a March into an area with opponent units triggers combat. The guidance uses triggersCombat flag to indicate. So likely it's empty.

We have to ensure supply. Stark's supply is 1 (as per observation; currently supply icons controlled =1). With supply 1, Stark can have at most some armies: according to supply track table (0 supply = 2 army sizes 2,2; 1 supply = 3,2,2). Our current supply track is at level 1, permitting armies of sizes 3,2,2,2? Wait table: For supply 1, permitted army sizes: 3,2. Probably two armies: one up to 3 units, one up to 2. Actually table says: Supply 0: 2,2 (two armies slots?). Supply 1: 3,2 (two slots). Supply 2: 3,2,2 (three slots). So at supply 1 we can have up to two armies: one with up to 3 units, another up to 2 units.

Our current units: at the-shivering-sea we have a ship. At white-harbor we have a footman (ID 3). At castle-black we have footman (1) and knight (2). At winterfell we have no units (since we moved them? Wait we moved footman & knight from winterfell to castle-black; that was previous action). So after that move, our units are: at castle-black (units 1 & 2), The Shivering Sea (unit 4), White Harbor (unit 3). Our supply: we have two armies? Let's see grouping: At castle-black, there are 2 units (footman+knight) in same land area => qualifies as an army (two or more units). That's an army of size 2.

The Shivering Sea has a ship alone, so it's a single unit, not an army.

White Harbor has a footman alone, single unit, not an army. So we have only one army (size 2). That's within supply (two armies allowed up to 3 and 2). Supply limit is fine.

If we move the ship from Shivering Sea to The Narrow Sea (sea). That would still be a single ship in a sea area. Not an army (size 1). That is fine.

If we move the footman from White Harbor to somewhere else, we need to check reachableRegions: those are castle-black, karhold, moat-cailin, widows-watch, winterfell. These are land areas. Some have castles (Moat Cailin has a castle (castle=1). The castle-black is no castle? Actually castle-black has castle=0 (just a name, not a castle). So we need to decide where to move footman. Also we have canLeavePowerToken: true for White Harbor (you can leave a power token). White Harbor currently has a castle (castle=1). The observation shows that White Harbor is a castle area for Stark, counting as a castle for victory points (controlledCastleAreas = 2 includes castle-black? Actually castle-black has castle=0, but Winterfell and Castle Black are the two castle areas? Wait Stark's controlled castle areas are 2. Which ones? Winterfell is a stronghold (castle=2) count as castle area? Home area with stronghold counts. Castle Black is not a castle (no castle icon). However winterfell is a stronghold (two). Also White Harbor is a castle area (castle=1). So probably those are the two castles: winterfell (stronghold) and White Harbor (castle). Also maybe castle-black is not a castle; but see map: castle-black is land area (presumably no castle icon). The castle area which is not a castle? anyway.

Thus White Harbor is a castle area (provides victory point). If we move the footman off White Harbor, we lose that castle unless we place a power token on White Harbor (leave_power_token true) to preserve control of White Harbor (since vacating). The guidance "canLeavePowerToken: true" indicates we may leave a power token. The question: Are we required to leave token to retain castle area? Yes: if you vacate a land area where you control a castle or stronghold, you can preserve control by leaving a power token (if you have one). If you leave, you must have enough power tokens (you have 5). So we can choose to leave power token, costing one power token, and we will keep White Harbor under our control (still counts as a castle area). That token remains there and continues to hold. We still control Winterfell, castle-black but it's not counting. So we need to decide whether to move footman out and if we leave token.

Potential moves: Move footman to Moat Cailin (castleLevel=1) which would capture a castle area (gain castle). That would be a new castle for Stark if it triggers combat? Wait Moat Cailin currently is neutral? The board for Moat Cailin: not listed in board entries; maybe neutral forces? The board's list doesn't include Moat Cailin but view may show no units. So it's probably empty (no units). It has a castle (castle=1). Moving footman there would vacate White Harbor (if we leave a token we stay in control) and capture Moat Cailin (control of a castle area). That would increase our castle count to 3? Actually we would control White Harbor (castle) and Moat Cailin (castle) plus Winterfell (stronghold). That's 3 areas. However note that White Harbor's castle would be under control via power token after the footman leaves. So that is beneficial.

But is moving footman to Moat Cailin legal? Check "canLeavePowerToken" true for White Harbor, but footman goes to Moat Cailin. That would be a move to a castle area. It should be allowed; check that moving to a castle area without enemy units means no combat (no battle). The actionGuidance lists reachableRegions; Moat Cailin is land, castleLevel 1, castleAreasGainedIfCaptured: 1, triggersCombat:false, so it's a direct capture.

One should also consider supply: moving footman to Moat Cailin creates a single unit there (unit alone) which is not an army. That is still within supply.

Now also move ship from Shivering Sea to The Narrow Sea (no combat). That will leave the Shivering Sea empty. Since it's a sea area, no need to place token. The ship will be alone in the narrow sea, still not an army.

Potentially we could also consider moving footman from White Harbor to Winterfell (Already Stark control). That would have no castle gain, but we would lose castle in White Harbor and may not keep token, thereby losing a castle. Not good.

Move footman to Karhold (no castle). Not beneficial.

Move footman to Widows Watch (no castle). Not beneficial.

Thus best is move footman from White Harbor to Moat Cailin, capture castle area, and leave power token on White Harbor to keep it.

Now we must consider: After moving footman, does White Harbor become vacant? Yes, we would vacate it. Since canLeavePowerToken is true, we can leave a token (must spend token). That token is placed there, preserving control. The token also would be used to retain control; we haven't used power tokens already this round (we have 5 available, but we must have at least 1 left). Yes.

Now we must also consider potential support for a combat if we moved footman into a location with enemy units. But Moat Cailin is empty, and "triggersCombat": false, so no combat.

Thus action chosen: Resolve March order for White Harbor (starting_region_id "white-harbor"), moves list with one destination: Moat Cailin, unit_ids [3] (footman). Also leave_power_token true (spend one power token). Additionally, we still have the other March order (the-shivering-sea) unresolved. The instruction says we have to choose which remaining March area to resolve now. We must submit an action for this decision only; we need to decide which region to resolve now. They give schema: starting_region_id must be either "the-shivering-sea" or "white-harbor". Moves can include up to 1 destination (maxItems = 1), i.e., only one destination group allowed. So choose "white-harbor" with the move.

Now we need to confirm the unit ID mapping: The footman at White Harbor is ID 3 (as per board: white-harbor units includes id:3, type footman). So unit_ids [3].

Now we need to ensure we meet the constraints: Must not exceed supply after moving. After moving, we'll have armies: Castle-black (2 units), Moat Cailin (1 footman alone), The Narrow Sea (ship alone). That's still only one army (castle-black) (size 2). So supply OK.

Now ensure we leave power token: We have power tokens 5. We need to leave a token on White Harbor. The action requires "leave_power_token": boolean. If true, we spend token. So must be true.

Now confirm there are no other constraints: "Each unit ID may be moved at most once." That's fine.

Now we should confirm that White Harbor's "castleAreasLostIfEmptiedWithoutToken":1 (as per actionGuidance). So leaving token avoids losing the castle.

Now move. Good.

Now final answer structure: JSON with starting_region_id "white-harbor", moves array with one object (destination_region_id "moat-cailin", unit_ids [3]), leave_power_token true.

Check that "moat-cailin" is spelled exactly as in reachableRegions: "moat-cailin". Yes case matches.

Now decide if we need to move any other units from White Harbor? Only footman ID 3.

Now confirm that "white-harbor" March order is March +0 (orderId 2). Our moving footman does not have any combat modifiers. The order's strength modification doesn't affect anything else.

Now final answer.

But we need to double-check that we have to keep leaving a power token on White Harbor only if we vacate it; we are vacating because footman leaves; but there might be any other units in White Harbor after moving? No. So token needed.

Now final answer JSON.

starting_region_id.description: Region containing the march order and moving units.
starting_region_id.title: Starting Region Id

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.
moves.title: Moves

leave_power_token.description: Spend one available power token to preserve control when legally vacating the source area. This must be false if units remain or control cannot be established.
leave_power_token.title: Leave Power Token

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. You choose which remaining March area to resolve now. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
